candidates.avoidWhen: more than 5 slices (AutoChart's own inference cap, `PIE_MAX_SLICES`) — use a bar or unit chart

candidates.name: RadarChart
candidates.matchedShape: several measures per entity, compared as an overall shape rather than value by value
candidates.avoidWhen: more than about 8 spokes, or absolute magnitude matters more than the shape

candidates.name: TreeChart
candidates.matchedShape: a hierarchy read as a branching tree rather than as sized rectangles
candidates.avoidWhen: size, not structure, is the point — use a treemap

candidates.name: HeatmapChart
candidates.matchedShape: one measure per calendar day over several months, as variant="calendar"
candidates.avoidWhen: fewer than about two months of days — too sparse to read as a calendar grid

query: a running total with signed steps into and out of it

candidates.name: WaterfallChart
candidates.matchedShape: a running total with signed steps into and out of it
candidates.avoidWhen: there is no meaningful running total — use diverging bars instead

candidates.name: BarChart
candidates.matchedShape: a single signed measure around a meaningful zero, as diverging bars with a zero line
candidates.avoidWhen: the zero baseline is not meaningful — plain bars read the same comparison

candidates.name: TreeChart
candidates.matchedShape: a metric decomposed into driver metrics — a KPI or driver tree
candidates.avoidWhen: size, not structure, is the point — use a treemap

candidates.name: ChoroplethChart
candidates.matchedShape: a measure by geographic region
candidates.avoidWhen: there is no real geography — use a bar chart

candidates.name: TreemapChart
candidates.matchedShape: a nested hierarchy sized by one measure
candidates.avoidWhen: the hierarchy has fewer than 2 levels — a flat bar chart is clearer
